newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices expected firm.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices expected firm.

text.p: Australian wool prices are likely to be generally firm this week with the possibility of some downside, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said in its weekly preview.

The eastern market indicator last week rose by one cent to 567 cents a kg clean, while the western market indicator rose four cents to 534 cents a kg clean. Sales this week are in Sydney, Geelong and Fremantle with 101,500 bales rostered.

Demand last week for fine and superfine wools was strong at the Goulburn sale but buyers were very selective with these types, Wesfarmers Dalgety said. The market may be tested this week by a relatively large offering at Geelong, it said.

Completion of the December stockpile requirement may provide more competition but the dramatic rise in the Australian dollar was expected to limit new Chinese orders. This would put some negative pressure on the broad end of the market, it said.

The Australian Council of Wool Exporters said last week's prices were satisfactory given the strengthening of the Australian dollar. While overall demand was "subdued", trade clearances were still up by 40 percent, or about 300,000 bales, on the corresponding period last season, it said.
The Wool Production Forecasting Committee meets on Thursday.
